newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian hockey in shock over sex assaults by coach.
newsitem.headline: Canadian hockey in shock over sex assaults by coach.

text.p: Canada's hockey world was in shock on Monday over revelations a junior hockey coach sexually abused two of his players, including a now professional player who has gone public with his story.

Graham James, long one of the pillars of Canada's junior, or teenage, hockey programme, received 3-1/2 years in jail after pleading guilty last Thursday to two counts of sexual assault against two ice hockey players.

The names of the victims were originally withheld under a court ban. The Toronto Star, however, published an interview on Monday with Sheldon Kennedy, now a forward with the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League.
Kennedy said he allowed his name to be used because he wanted the public to help prevent the kind of abuse he suffered over a 12-year period with James.
"This is the hardest bloody thing I have ever had to work and deal with in my life, and it will be the hardest thing I will ever have to deal with," Kennedy told the Star.

James was found guilty of two counts of sexual assault involving more than 300 sexual encounters over six years with one man and 50 more encounters with another man over four years. The incidents, sometimes at the coach's home, began in 1984 and ended in 1995. They started when one victim was as young as 14.
James had held several high-profile positions in the amateur hockey ranks, including most recently general manager and coach of the Western Hockey League's Calgary Hitmen in Alberta.
He resigned in September when news of the police investigation began. The probe, which is still continuing, started after one of the victims came forward.
James, 42, read a statement to the court after his sentencing: "I preached selflessness, yet I ended up being selfish ... I'm truly sorry this happened."
There has been widespread shock that the crimes had been hushed up for so long and much anger over the fact James could be eligible for parole as early as this September.
Don Cherry, a well-known hockey commentator and former coach of the Boston Bruins, exploded on national television, calling James a "creep" for preying on a young boy.
"If I had been the judge I'd have drawn and quartered the s.o.b.," Cherry said.

Kennedy said in the newspaper interview he gradually came under the control of his coach, who used a variety of tactics including verbal abuse and even a shotgun to coerce him into regular encounters that included oral sex and masturbation.

"I feel like I am 10 months old inside a 27-year-old body, Kennedy said. "You are learning to live again. You are learning to have friends and you have to learn to love and relax. I can't remember the last day I relaxed totally."

Mick Mitrovic, president of the eastern region of the Canadian Professional Hockey School, said he was not surprised when he heard about the conviction because there had been cases and rumours about problems with coaches and players before.
But he was surpised how long the abuse continued before it was brought to the attention of the police.
"It just goes to show you they are kids and they are subject to things that even young adults are not ready for," Mitrovic said.
